To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the novel micelle/ precursor co-templating method is developed for the synthesis of ultrasmall MONs with a large pore size, which are further used for intranuclear gene therapy.
a micelle/precursors co-templating strategy was developed to synthesize a large pore ultrasmall meso-porous organosilicas (MONs) with a high loading capacity and improved gene protection.

a novel micelle/ precursor co-templating strategy is developed to prepare large-pore ultramall mesoporous silica nanoparticles, which exhibit a high loading efficiency and a good protection for the loaded genes, and the elaborately designed MON-PTAT shows a high transfection efficiency for the pEGFP plasmid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of large-pore ultrastable mesoporous organo-silica nanoparticles with a high surface area and a high pore volume.
the synthesis of large-pore ultralightweight MONs, which have a high loading capacity for the delivery of DNA and a high transfection efficiency.
the synthesis of large-pore ultramall MONs with high loading capacity and the development of an efficient gene delivery system based on the large-pore ultrammall MONs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MONs-PTAT can be used as a promising gene carrier for intranuclear gene transfection.
MONs-PTAT are promising candidates for intranuclear gene transfection.
the present study provides a novel and effective strategy for the synthesis of large-pore ultrastable MONs, which may be promising for a broad range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the micelle/precursory co-templating strategy is a promising approach to synthesize large pore MONs with a small particle size and high surface area, and the MONs-PTAT are a new type of non-viral vector with a large loading capacity, good stability and high transfection efficiencies.

we have successfully synthesized the large-pore ultramall mesoporous silica nanoparticles (LUMs) with the help of the co-assembly of the cationic surfactant cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and the anionic precursor N,N-dimethyldodecyl-3-(trimethoxysilyl)-propylammonium bromine (DDA-Si).
the large-pore ultramsall mesoporous MONs are successfully synthesized by a micelle/precusor co-templating strategy and they are promising for nuclear-targeted gene delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the large pore size and ultrasmall size of the MONs are critical for the efficient nuclear delivery of genes, which can be used for the design of novel gene delivery systems.
the large-pore ultramall MONs can be synthesized by using the micelle/precusor co-templating method.

the large-pore ultramall mesoporous nanoparticles with the size of less than 100 nm can be synthesized by a novel micelle/ precursor co-templating strategy, which is a promising candidate for gene delivery.
